details.label: Summary
details.text: The cluster of storms has undergone general weakening, but could still pose a risk for strong to severe wind gusts along and south of the I-80 corridor, east of Des Moines toward the Mississippi River, through 9-10 AM CDT

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Coldest cloud tops in infrared satellite imagery and peak lightning flash rates have generally been maintained into the Des Moines vicinity, but the convective system has become less organized looking in radar loops. The primary MCV and westerly rear inflow to its southwest have undergone recent weakening. However, another notable cyclonic circulation has developed to the east-southeast (now to the northeast of Des Moines), within continuing stronger thunderstorm development focused near/above the leading edge of a developing area of 2-hourly surface pressure rises on the order of 2 mb. This may continue pose the most prominent risk for a swath of strong to severe surface gusts near the I-80 corridor east of Des Moines through 14-15Z. It does not appear out of the question that another similar circulation could still evolve within trailing convection now to the southwest through south of Des Moines
